 Following September’s heavy month of smart home launches , I didn’t expect October to be able to keep up. But if anything, October might have beaten the previous month – here’s what you might have missed.
 The biggest thing to come from October was the Apple ‘Welcome Home’ event which finally announced new smart products from the brand, including a new version of its HomePod mini, Apple 4K TV and the long-awaited HomeView.
 Not one to be outdone, Amazon also announced a new Echo smart speaker line-up, and its Ring and Blink companies also debuted new security camera collections. It’s been a whirlwind of a month, so here are 10 of the best smart home launches from October 2026.
 Latest Videos From T3 
 Watch full video here: 
 Apple HomeView
 (Image credit: Apple)
 As mentioned, Apple announced a fleet of new smart devices, including the Apple HomeView , its new smart home hub with a 7-inch touchscreen, built-in speaker and Siri AI. It comes in two versions – a tabletop with a speaker base, and a wall-mounted option.
 The Apple HomeView is powered by the Apple A18 chip , and can be paired with compatible Apple Intelligence-enabled devices. It can recognise up to six people, and has access to lots of smart home controls and apps, including Apple Music, FaceTime, Podcast and more. It’s available to pre-order at £299 / $299 with shipping expected in November.
 You may like
 10 smart home launches from September 2026, including Eufy, Philips Hue, Tado, Aqara and more 
 7 smart home launches from August 2026, featuring EcoFlow, Philips Hue, Govee and more 
 Apple 'Welcome Home' event recap: New HomeView, HomePod mini, Apple TV and more 
 Amazon’s new Echo speaker line-up
 (Image credit: Amazon)
 Towards the end of October, Amazon announced a new Echo speaker line-up , featuring a new version of the Echo Dot, as well as a Kids edition. The newer products include the Echo Time and the Echo Studio with Home Camera.
 The Echo Studio with Home Camera is an upgraded version of the Echo Studio, and features a 13-megapixel camera. It has Alexa + and Live View so you can check in on your home while you’re away, and it has powerful 3D sound. The Echo Time is a camera-free Echo – similar to the Echo Spot – that acts as a smart alarm clock.
 Sign up to the T3 newsletter for smarter living straight to your inbox
 Get all the latest news, reviews, deals and buying guides on gorgeous tech, home and active products from the T3 experts
 Ring 4K & 2K cameras
 (Image credit: Ring)
 As an Amazon-owned company, Ring has also had a big product launch in October by introducing five new security cameras . The models include indoor and outdoor models, and use 4K or 2K video resolution to clearly capture images around your home.
 Installation is the biggest upgrade with the new Ring cameras. Its Ring Outdoor Camera 4K Plus has been described as its most flexible option yet, as it can be set-up via battery, wired, solar, plug-in or Power-over-Ethernet. The cameras are available to pre-order with shipping expected in November.
 Blink 4K & 2K cameras
 (Image credit: Blink)
 Yet another Amazon company with new product launches, Blink also dropped five new security cameras to the UK and US. The UK launches include Blink’s first 4K wired security camera and a pan-tilt zoom camera, while the US launches include spotlight, outdoor and frontier models.
 What to read next
 Apple's Home Collection brings new smart home gadgets to the UK this December 
 All-new Apple device coming 13 October, along with the long-awaited new Apple TV 4K – claims an expert in the know 
 Apple's new smart home lineup is coming as 'Welcome Home' event confirmed for 13th October 
 The standout for the UK launches is the Blink Mini 4K+ which has Blink’s highest resolution yet. It can be used both indoors and outdoors – although it is a plug-in model – and has 115-degree horizontal views and 10x enhanced zoom. For the US, the Blink Frontier XR+ is the brand’s farthest-reaching camera to date and is designed for use as a trail camera for remote locations.
 Arlo Essential Solar Security Camera 
 (Image credit: Arlo)
 It’s all about security cameras this month – as you’ll see with the rest of this list! – and Arlo dropped its new Essential Solar Security Camera in early October – but only in the US. With an ultra-slim design, the camera takes up minimal space and blends seamlessly into the background.
 The main standout of the Arlo Essential Solar Security Camera is its integrated 1.2W solar panel and high-powered battery that can keep the camera charged for up to six months without any sun. At $99.99, it’s not too expensive, either.
 EZVIZ CB30 Dual Kit
 (Image credit: EZVIZ)
 EZVIZ’s new CB30 Dual Kit is a solar-powered outdoor security camera with a strange, robot-like design. It looks like E.T. and connects to an oversized solar panel to ensure constant charging via solar energy.
 The EZVIZ CB30 Dual Kit features dual lenses for enhanced coverage, and 3K 5MP resolution for crystal clear images. It also has three built-in spotlights to illuminate your home, and to scare off potential intruders. Similar to Arlo, it’s only £99.99, and at launch, it was discounted so it’s a great budget-friendly option.
 Reolink OMVI 2i Ultra
 (Image credit: Reolink)
 The Reolink OMVI 2i Ultra was announced at IFA 2026 , and finally became available to buy this month. Another solar-powered camera, the Reolink OMVI 2i Ultra is wire-free and has two camera lenses to cover your entire home, without missing any action or blind spots.
 The Reolink OMVI 2i Ultra combines an 8MP wide-angle camera with a 5MP pan-and-tilt camera, and uses Reolink's SyncTrack technology to lower camera to continue following a detected person or object after they move out of the wide-angle camera's view.
 Tapo C550WS
 (Image credit: Tapo)
 The last security camera launch worth knowing about from October, the Tapo C550WS is the brand’s latest outdoor security camera with 4K resolution . Alongside 4K recording, the camera has 360° coverage, colour night vision and AI detection to keep your home safe, and you in the know.
 The most impressive part of the Tapo C550WS is its red-blue light and sound alarm. It’s equipped with a 110dB siren that, when triggered, sounds off loudly and flashes with red and blue lights to scare off unwanted visitors.
 Govee Outdoor Deck Lights 2 
 (Image credit: Govee)
 Moving into smart lighting , Govee announced the second generation of its Outdoor Deck Lights. Currently available in the US for $119.99, the Govee Outdoor Deck Lights 2 are brighter than before, and more water-resistant with an IP67 rating.
 The Govee Outdoor Deck Lights 2 include individual smart lights designed to be mounted on walls or fences . Alongside practical lighting, you can change the brightness, and choose from 16 million colours, music-sync effects and over 100 lighting scenes.
 SwitchBot Permanent Outdoor Lights
 (Image credit: SwitchBot)
 Another outdoor lighting set, the SwitchBot Permanent Outdoor Lights are designed for year round use, and offer native Matter over Wi-Fi support. Measuring 30 metres, the light strip features 72 evenly-spaced LEDs, and can be installed in your home’s eaves, balconies, garages, patios and walkways.
 Like Govee, the SwitchBot Permanent Outdoor Lights come with 16 million colour options, and use an RGBIC+WW design which combines RGB colours, warm-white and cool-white lights .

results.title: Blink Solar Panel Mount Overview — Blink Support
results.text:
Blink Solar Panel Mount Overview — Blink Support 
 Support Home 
 Accessories 
 Solar Panel Mount 
 Blink Solar Panel Mount Overview 
 The Blink Solar Panel is a solar shade mount for the Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera. Other Blink outdoor cameras (Outdoor 4, XT or XT2) are not supported. The low power consumption technology makes this a great option for outdoor camera mounting and is weather-resistant. Solar powering your Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) gives you a powerful wireless security camera system anywhere on your property, with a motion detection range of approximately 6 - 20 feet (2m to 6m).
 The camera snaps into a mount in the bottom of the unit and connects to a weather-resistant micro USB cable. On the top, a solar panel attaches to a mount and can be adjusted +/- 10 degrees horizontally or vertically to optimize sun exposure, or it can be detached for placement in direct sunlight up to 2 ft. away, using the provided accessory mount.
 What's in the Box
 The solar panel packaging includes:
 Mounts for Blink Camera and Solar Panel (not removable)
 Micro-USB power cord (not removable)
 1 Detachable wall mounting plate (slide down to remove)
 1 Detachable Solar Panel with 2 ft. cord
 1 Preinstalled 3.7V 18650 (3200mAh) lithium-ion battery
 Screws and Anchors for Mounting (4 each)
 1 Volcano mount
 1 Housing cover
 User Manual
 13 ft. extension micro-USB cable (sold separately)

 Blink Solar Panel Mount Overview 
 The Blink Solar Panel is a solar shade mount for the Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera. Other Blink outdoor cameras (Outdoor 4, XT or XT2) are not supported. The low power consumption technology makes this a great option for outdoor camera mounting, and it is weather resistant. Solar powering your Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) gives you a powerful wireless security camera system anywhere on your property, with a motion detection range of approximately 6–20 feet (2–6 m).
 The camera snaps into a mount at the bottom of the unit and connects to a weather-resistant micro-USB cable. At the top, a solar panel attaches to a mount and can be adjusted +/- 10 degrees horizontally or vertically to optimise sun exposure, or it can be detached for placement in direct sunlight up to 2 ft (60 cm) away using the provided accessory mount.
 What’s in the Box?
 The Solar Panel packaging includes:
 Mounts for Blink Camera and Solar Panel (not removable)
 Micro-USB power cable (not removable)
 1 Detachable wall mounting plate (slide down to remove)
 1 Detachable Solar Panel with 2 ft (60 cm) cable
 1 Preinstalled 3.7V 18650 (3200mAh) lithium-ion battery
 Screws and Anchors for Mounting (4 each)
 1 Volcano mount
 1 Housing cover
 User Manual
 13 ft (4 m) extension micro-USB cable (sold separately)

results.title: Blink Solar Panel Mount FAQ — Blink Support
results.text:
Blink Solar Panel Mount FAQ — Blink Support 
 Support Home 
 Accessories 
 Solar Panel Mount 
 Blink Solar Panel Mount FAQ 
 The following are commonly asked questions about the Blink Solar Panel Mount.
 What is the Blink Solar Panel Mount?
 The Blink Solar Panel Mount is a wireless solar panel charging accessory that uses sunlight to power the Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) Camera (Outdoor 4, XT and XT2 not supported).
 Delete 
 How does the Blink Solar Panel Mount work?
 First remove the pull-tab in the battery compartment to activate the battery. Next, you simply plug the camera in via the Micro-USB cord, then snap the camera onto the mount. After a few minutes, the camera will then be able to access the rechargeable battery built into the solar panel. Click here  for detailed setup instructions.
 Delete 
 Why don't I see "External Power OK" as the Battery status in the Camera Settings?
 This may occur for the following reasons:
 The battery tab has not been removed from the compartment (located on the back of the unit) which prevents them from charging.
 It takes three minutes for the unit to check for a change in voltage on the USB line after the camera is connected.
 It is sometimes necessary for the camera to first detect motion or perform a live view in order for the power status to update in the app.
 Delete 
 Can I use the Solar Panel Mount with any Blink Cameras?
 No, the Solar Mount can only be used with Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) cameras. Other Blink outdoor cameras (Outdoor 4, XT or XT2) are NOT compatible with its Micro-USB connector to provide a weather resistant seal.
 Delete 
 Does my Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera have full functionality when powered by the Solar Panel Mount?
 Yes, as long as your camera receives adequate power from the Solar Panel Mount it will have full functionality, exactly the same as when it's powered by the camera's 2 AA 1.5 volt batteries. It is important; however, to keep functional batteries in your camera, in case your solar panel battery has no charge.
 Delete 
 Will my camera use its internal batteries if the Solar Panel Mount has no charge?
 Yes, your Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) Camera will switch to using its internal 1.5v AA lithium batteries in the event that your Solar Panel Mount has no charge. Once your Mount has adequate charge to power your camera, it will revert back to using it after three minutes or upon the execution of a new event (ex. Live View or Motion Detection).
 Delete 
 Does the Solar Panel charge my camera batteries?
 No, the Solar Panel simply provides external power to your Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) Camera, which may extend the life of your camera's batteries.
 Delete 
 What kind of battery is used in the Blink Solar Panel Mount?
 The Solar Panel uses one 18650 Lithium-Ion rechargeable battery. In the event a new battery is required, please only use an 18650 battery with the following specifications: 3.7 V, 3200mAh, 11.84Wh.
 Delete 
 Where can I mount my Blink Solar Panel Mount?
 The Solar Panel Mount can be mounted on various surfaces including siding, stone, and wood. It can be installed in both wall and eave orientations. Wherever the solar panel is mounted, it is important to place your Solar Panel Mount in south facing direction to receive optimal sunlight and maintain its charge. Click here  for detailed instructions on how to mount the Blink Solar Panel.
 Delete 
 Is the Solar Panel adjustable to position for optimal sunlight?
 Yes, the Solar Panel Mount can be adjusted by pivoting or detaching the solar panel to capture optimal sunlight in a remote mounted location. Click here  for detailed specifications regarding camera and solar panel tilt ranges.
 Delete 
 What if my preferred mounting position does not have access to sunlight?
 To allow for Solar Panel mounting in a position which receives more sun exposure, you can remove the panel from the housing to access the 2ft long cable for better positioning. A 13 ft long extension weatherproof cable can be purchased separately to further extend the Solar Panel for optimal sunlight charging. This will allow for the panel to be positioned further from the mounting bracket, in ideal sunlight conditions. If the solar panel is removed, a solar panel cavity cover can be snapped onto the mount; protecting inside the mount from water and debris.
 Click here  to purchase the 13 ft weatherproof extension cable in the US or click here  to purchase in Canada.
 Delete 
 If the Blink Solar Panel is fully detached for external mounting, is it protected against weather?
 Yes, the Blink Solar Panel can be protected against water and debris when the included Solar Panel housing is placed securely.
 Delete 
 Is the Micro USB cable removable so I can install a longer cable?
 No, the attached micro-USB cable for the Blink Solar Panel Mount and the Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) Camera connection is not removable. You can purchase a 13 ft weatherproof extension cable (sold separately) if you wish to detach and mount the Solar Panel up to 15 ft away from your camera.
 Delete 
 Is the Blink Solar Panel Mount weather resistant?
 Yes, the Solar Panel Mount is IP65 certified weather resistant. There are two drainage holes on the base of the housing to allow water entering the housing to pass by the camera on both sides.
 Delete 
 What is the operating temperature range of the Blink Solar Panel Mount?
 The Solar Panel Mount operating temperate range is between -4°F to 113°F (-20 to 45°C).
 Delete 
 Does the Blink Solar Panel have a warranty?
 Yes, the Blink Solar Panel has a 1-year limited warranty (2 years for EU/UK). To learn more about Blink's Limited Warranty .
 Delete

results.title: How to Set Up the Blink Solar Panel Mount — Blink Support
results.text:
How to Set Up the Blink Solar Panel Mount — Blink Support 
 Support Home 
 Accessories 
 Solar Panel Mount 
 How to Set Up the Blink Solar Panel Mount 
 The following easy steps explain how to install and configure your Blink Solar Panel Mount. You must first have a fully functional Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera set up in your Blink account, before attaching the camera to the mount. In addition, the lithium batteries must remain in your outdoor camera before connecting it to the solar panel mount. Other Blink outdoor cameras (Outdoor 4, XT or XT2) are not supported. 
 Click here  for instructions on how to add your Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera to your account.
1. Detach the mounting bracket from the back of the Solar Panel by pulling down on the bracket. After the bracket is removed, you will be able to easily remove the plastic wrap from the Solar Panel Mount.
2. Remove the pull-tab from the battery compartment (located on the back of the unit) by removing the screws on the left and right sides. This tab protects the battery during shipping and must be removed in order to power your device.
 Once the plastic tab is removed, screw the cover back in place before installation.
 3. Completely remove the back and USB port covers from your Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera. Removing the USB cover will ensure you have an optimal weather resistant seal between the micro-USB cable and your camera.
Once the USB cover is fully removed, reattached the back cover on your Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera. Click here  to learn more about how to remove and attach the back cover on your Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera.
 4. Next, firmly plug the micro-USB cable into your outdoor camera, making certain that you have a tight seal on all sides . 
 5 . Snap the camera onto the front mount.
6 . You also have the option of using a snap-in cover which protects the interior from the elements when the solar panel is placed in a remote location as shown below.
 A separate volcano mount is included for mounting the solar panel in a remote location.
7 . Attach the Mounting Plate to an exterior wall that has direct sunlight exposure. The plate can be mounted with two screws (and anchors if needed). You may also take advantage of no-drill installation and hang the plate with vinyl siding hooks (not provided).
 The tabs on the mounting plate insert into the slots on the back of the Solar Panel Mount and are secured by pushing them down into place.
When you have the unit mounted in an optimal location, the solar panel and camera can be adjusted at different angles and rotated as needed.
In the Blink app you will see External Power  as "OK" for the status in the Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera's settings, once the batteries in the Solar Panel Mount have a charge. Your Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera is then ready for use.
 One of the most important considerations when installing your Blink Solar Panel Mount is placing it so it gets adequate sunlight to maintain its charge year-round. You should also take into consideration that you are not completely dependent on the sun to keep your camera operational. Once your mount has adequate charge to power your camera, your camera will revert back to using it.
 By ensuring your lights are mounted with a clear view of the sun’s rays, you will maintain a steady charge rate during the day. Your solar panel should also be facing south towards the equator, which is even more important during winter months when the days are shorter with less sunlight. Solar powering your Blink Outdoor (3rd Gen) camera provides you with a reliable and powerful wireless security camera system, once you have the optimal sun exposure on your mount.
